messages:
maria: CI red on master, failing flake in runtime tests again. Job: https://ci.redwood.example/job/serve-runtime/4432 — test name: TestAdaptiveBatchAllocator::test_allocator_race. Failure seems timing-y, logs attached.
ci-bot: job 4432 failed on shard 7. failing test: tests/runtime/test_allocator.py::TestAdaptiveBatchAllocator::test_allocator_race
ci-bot: last 200 lines:
```
E       AssertionError: expected 4 batches, got 3
...
Allocator::choose_batch_size at src/runtime/allocator.cc:412
std::shuffle at /usr/include/c++/random:123
```
sam: thanks — can you paste the failing stdout and the env used? seed, workers, any CI overrides?
maria: pasted logs to the job artifacts and attached a small gist with the failing output. env: TEST_WORKERS=4, CI_RNG_SEED unset, CI_PARALLEL=3. No special overrides.
jordan: this looks nondeterministic. try running locally with a fixed seed: TEST_RNG_SEED=12345 pytest tests/runtime/test_allocator.py::TestAdaptiveBatchAllocator::test_allocator_race -k allocator_race -q
ashish: also try limiting threads to 1 to rule out parallel teardown: OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
maria: ran locally with seed=12345 + OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and reproduced once. output: same assert (expected 4 batches). Running again with seed=6789 passed.
sam: ok that matches a seed-dependent flake. can you run bisect to find when it regressed? we merged the batching reorder PR last week.
maria: starting bisection with our bisect script: ./scripts/ci/bisect_flake.sh --test tests/runtime/test_allocator.py::TestAdaptiveBatchAllocator::test_allocator_race --good SHA_a1b2 --bad HEAD
ci-bot: bisection started, will post updates.
devops: if you want a quicker confirmation, you can also trigger a rerun of the single failing shard from the job UI (re-run failed stage). saves time vs full bisection.
maria: bisect found first bad commit: 18f3c9d — "batch reorder: prefer epoch-aware packing"
rachel: that PR changed iteration order in the packing loop, used std::shuffle in a faster path. likely introduced reliance on RNG order.
jordan: probable root: packing used unordered container + shuffle + vector iteration which made non-deterministic ties. Two options: make packing deterministic (stable sort by key) or seed RNG deterministically in tests.
nashish: prefer making production behavior deterministic where possible. Tests relying on implementation order are brittle. If shuffle is necessary for fairness, use RNGState from runtime seeded by an explicit config value and default to nondeterministic only in hosted mode.
maria: for immediate unblock I'll add a test-only env guard: if TEST_RNG_SEED set then seed global RNG from it. also adding a short sleep in the test to reduce race surface while we do a proper fix.
sam: please don't add sleeps to prod code. test-only sleep is fine as temporary. open a tracking issue to revert.
maria: agreed — will open PR with two commits: (1) test: set RNG seed when TEST_RNG_SEED present + small 10ms sleep in test rerun block, (2) runtime: make packer use stable sort for deterministic ordering + add unit to assert stable order invariant.
jordan: can you include the failing seed in PR description (repro: TEST_RNG_SEED=94213)?
maria: will do. repro seed is 94213. bisect script also captured stack trace and minimal reproduction.
nashish: assign me as reviewer once PR is up. also include perf note — stable sort change could affect latencies in tight loops; include benchmark.
rachel: if perf hit is non-trivial we can gate stable behavior behind a config flag and enable deterministic mode in CI. but prefer a correctness-first patch.
devbot: reminder — follow the patch checklist: link issue, add changelog, add unit, run perf test suite.
maria: creating PR now and assigning reviewers @ashish @jordan. PR link: https://git.redwood.example/runtime/pulls/772
sam: great, thanks. once merged let's trigger a full CI run and mark the issue as flaky->fixed. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks all — will update here with merge and CI green. :eyes:
